sections.h2: What are a Mableton seller's choices?
sections.html:
Sellers in Mableton can put the house on the market with an agent, handle the sale alone, or take an as-is offer, weighing repair costs against the date they need to move. Voters in this south Cobb County community approved cityhood on November 8, 2022, and the first council was chosen at a March 21, 2023 election.

By the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate the city holds 78,820 people, measured from an April 2020 base of 77,077. With that many people, buyers are plentiful and so are competing listings, which puts condition and price first.

sections.h2: How do Mableton households look in Census data?
sections.html:
Census data covering 2020 through 2024 shows 29,109 households, 64.6 percent of them owners. The median home is worth $313,100, owners with a mortgage typically spend $1,777 a month, and gross rent runs about $1,472.

  • Household income, typical: $77,980 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Stayed at the same address for a year: 88.1 percent
  • Adults with at least a bachelor's degree: 38.7 percent
  • Average commute: 30.7 minutes

With nearly nine in ten residents unmoved from one year to the next, many sellers on established streets have owned for a long time.

sections.h2: Where is Mableton and what is its history?
sections.html:
Mableton lies about 15 miles west-northwest of Atlanta and about 20 miles from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. The Chattahoochee River marks the southeast edge, with Smyrna to the north and Austell to the west. The Silver Comet Trail, a 61.5-mile paved path starting in Smyrna, crosses Floyd Road in Mableton.

Cherokee and Creek communities held this land before settlers arrived. A depot opened in December 1881 on the line that became Norfolk Southern, and a post office came in 1882, turning Mableton into the trading point for rural Cobb. The town was chartered in 1912 and lost that charter in 1916, after a flood swamped its sewer system and residents won a county-wide drainage tax. A century of unincorporated life followed until the 2022 vote.

Cobb County's school district operates the public schools. Elementary schools in the area include Mableton, Clay-Harmony Leland, Bryant, Riverside, Russell and City View, and middle schools include Floyd, Garrett, Lindley and Betty Gray. Pebblebrook and South Cobb are the high schools. The South Cobb Regional Library serves the community, and The SAE School teaches preschool through eighth grade.

Assignment follows the address, so check it with the district before naming a school in your listing.

sections.h2: What else shapes the Mableton neighborhood?
sections.html:
Fulton County Airport, known as Brown Field, touches Mableton's southeast border with two runways and about 65,000 operations a year, so a house on that side may hear aircraft. The Census Bureau lists 3,919 veterans in the city, 17.6 percent foreign-born residents and 26.1 percent of people over age five speaking another language at home. The South Cobb area also hosts a part-time Georgia Japanese Language School.

Retail sales for 2022 reached about $409 million, and 72.9 percent of adults 16 and over are in the labor force. A buyer who works nearby, along the Silver Comet Trail or toward Smyrna, may value the commute more than finishes.

sections.h2: What new development is changing Mableton?
sections.html:
County planning documents describe a Mableton Town Center vision for the Mableton Parkway area, formalized after a 2010 design week and approved by the Cobb Board of Commissioners in 2013. Later projects included a 31-acre mixed-use plaza near Mableton Parkway and Old Powder Springs Road with townhomes, courtyard cottages and detached houses, and a 60-acre redevelopment along Floyd Road with apartments and townhomes approved on October 21, 2020.

For a seller, new construction nearby can raise buyer interest in the area while also giving buyers newer alternatives. Price against what is actually for sale on your street, not against the plan documents.

sections.h2: How are Mableton property taxes billed?
sections.html:
The city has no general property tax. Cobb County keeps billing county and school taxes, and Mableton sends separate bills for its special service districts. Cobb's 2026 bills were issued in August with a due date of October 15, 2026, and the assessor, who values property at 40 percent of market, mailed 2026 notices on June 5.

The city's Public Safety Special Services District covers the cost of police services the city took over from Cobb on June 1, 2025. The city began billing it in October 2026 at 4.5 mills, applied to the assessed value set by Cobb. A separate Six Flags Special Services District has been billed by the city since October 2025.

sections.h2: How should I handle both bills at a Mableton closing?
sections.html:
Ask your closing attorney or the title company to pull the Cobb bill and each city district bill, since a buyer will ask how every one was settled. Your sales contract decides who pays which share of the year.

The city applies its millage to the assessed value Cobb sets. Ask the city finance office for the district bill's due date, and keep proof of payment for the closing file. Cobb's 2026 announcement adds that the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant appears as a separate reduction on eligible bills, and that anyone who loses homestead eligibility must tell the Tax Commissioner.

sections.h2: What happens to a homestead exemption when I sell?
sections.html:
Cobb's assessor calls it a break for owners who live in the house as a primary residence, and listed July 20 as the 2026 filing deadline. An owner who is no longer eligible must report it before the appeal deadline or owe the back taxes and interest plus a 50 percent penalty on the amount wrongly reduced.

After a sale, make sure the Tax Commissioner and your closing attorney know the house stopped being your primary residence at transfer.

sections.h2: What permits and rules apply to Mableton houses?
sections.html:
Mableton's Building Division reviews plans against Georgia's minimum standard codes, inspects work and issues Certificates of Occupancy. Applications go through the online CloudPermit portal only; emailed ones are refused. Crews may work 7 AM to 7 PM weekdays and 9 AM to 5 PM Saturdays, never on Sundays or designated holidays.

  • Collect permits and final inspection records for recent work.
  • Ask the general contractor to confirm each inspection passed.
  • If the home was rented, ask the city's Business License office whether any registration is still active.

sections.h2: What deed transfer tax applies in Mableton?
sections.html: Georgia prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. The contract may place it on the buyer, and the deed cannot be recorded with the court clerk until it is paid.

faqs.q: Does Mableton levy a city property tax?
faqs.a: There is no general city levy. Mableton bills a Public Safety district at 4.5 mills, which began in October 2026, and a Six Flags district it has billed since October 2025. Cobb still bills county and school taxes.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Cobb tax due date for Mableton owners?
faqs.a: October 15, 2026, received by the Tax Commissioner's Office or postmarked by USPS that day.

faqs.q: How long can I contest my Cobb value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days after the date printed on the Notice of Assessment. The city adds that a parcel with an appeal pending receives a temporary bill at 85 percent of assessed value until it is settled.

faqs.q: Who sets property values inside Mableton?
faqs.a: Cobb County. The city says values come from Cobb and appeals go to the Cobb Board of Tax Assessors, which also oversees homestead filings.

faqs.q: Can a Mableton house in poor repair be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, as is, to a buyer who accepts the condition, or after fixes with a listing. Keep permit records for earlier work so title review does not stall the closing.
